reason: Recovered-branch ARCHIVE, not live code: 18 snapshots of test files from abandoned branches, several of them older copies of files that still exist elsewhere in the tree. Running them would assert against code that was deliberately not merged. Excluded at the bunfig.toml pathIgnorePatterns layer, so bun cannot discover them from any invocation; this entry is the written half of that exclusion.

MEASURED 2026-08-13, reproduced twice: runHealthCheck probes the live repository over the network, and its single test times out after 60s, carrying the file to 93s wall-clock and failing. The other 50 tests in the file pass in under a second. It is a live-environment probe wearing a unit-test name, so it cannot join the PR lane until that one test is separated or gated. Losing 50 real assertions to keep it out is a genuine cost, recorded here rather than hidden.

MEASURED on ubuntu-24.04 in PR #10473 run 31757721615: 7 failures, each asserting that a persona agent CLI is on PATH (claude, kiro-cli, codex, cursor-agent, agy). Those exist on the maintainer workstation and on no runner, so the file measures the HOST rather than the code. Passes on a developer machine, fails in CI by construction.

MEASURED on ubuntu-24.04 in PR #10473 run 31757721615: 2 failures in detectGreyTextMacOS, which shells osascript. That binary is macOS-only, so the tests cannot pass on a Linux runner and cannot be made to without a platform guard inside the file. This is genuine three-way-parity DEBT, not a permanent exclusion: the same file passes on the dev laptop and fails in CI, which is drift by definition.

MEASURED on ubuntu-24.04 in PR #10473 run 31757721615: all 6 tests fail with Expected claimed, Received wait-pr-capacity. The suite queries the LIVE pull-request queue, so its result depends on how many PRs happen to be open at the moment it runs. That makes it nondeterministic in any lane, CI or laptop; it passed locally only because the queue was quiet. A test whose verdict tracks repository weather is not a unit test.

HARDWARE-ONLY LANE. The only reason it is excluded is that no runner has the silicon: the PKCS#11 tests need an attached token holding an AES-256 key labelled zeta-frost-wrap, and the TPM 2.0 tests need a TPM device node plus tpm2-tools. This entry REPLACES the previous exclusion of frost-share-adapter.test.ts, whose own reason named separating the platform-specific test as the fix. That separation is now done and the CI-safe file runs in the gate with 16 tests. Non-vacuity is enforced INSIDE this file rather than promised here: selecting a lane via ZETA_FROST_HARDWARE_LANE asserts that hardware is attached, so opting in without it FAILS rather than skips, an unrecognised lane name FAILS, and no code path in the file constructs the software fake. MEASURED 2026-08-13 on darwin-arm64: lane tpm2 gives 2 failures because Apple Silicon has no TPM 2.0, lane pkcs11 gives 2 failures because no token is attached, and lane tpm gives 1 failure because the name is unrecognised. CORRECTED 2026-08-23: that MEASURED line was no longer reproducible by the command the file documented. Because this path is in bunfig.toml's pathIgnorePatterns, and bun applies pathIgnorePatterns even to an EXPLICIT path filter, `bun test ./tools/setup/persona-keys/frost-share-adapter.hardware.test.ts` returned 'The following filters did not match any test files' and exit 1 -- the same exit status a correctly-running lane returns when the token is absent, so the operator could not tell 'no token' from 'the lane never ran'. The exclusion here is right; what was missing was a way to reach the lane deliberately. bunfig.hardware-lane.toml is that escape hatch, and the invocation is `bun --config=bunfig.hardware-lane.toml test <path>` -- the flag must precede the subcommand, since `bun test --config=X` parses and ignores X. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 on darwin-arm64 with that invocation and no token attached: 2 failures (HW-1, HW-2), 1 pass, 13 tests -- the fail-rather-than-skip behaviour this entry claims. Reachability is now pinned by MLANE-12..15 in src/Core.TypeScript/zflash/usb-hardware-manual-lane.test.ts.
